official_measurement_examples.name: Mandatory licensing occupation threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK guidance states mandatory HMO licensing generally applies where 5 or more people from more than 1 household occupy the HMO, subject to the statutory definition and local scheme context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Licence duration ceiling
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK states an HMO licence is valid for a maximum of 5 years and a separate licence is needed for each HMO operated.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2018 scope extension
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2018 prescribed-description reform removed the former three-storey limitation for mandatory licensing of qualifying HMOs from 1 October 2018.

official_measurement_examples.name: Minimum single-adult sleeping room
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2018 mandatory-conditions regulations set 6.51 square metres as the national minimum sleeping room floor area for one person aged over 10 in licensed Part 2 HMOs.

official_measurement_examples.name: Minimum two-person sleeping room
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2018 regulations set 10.22 square metres as the national minimum sleeping room floor area for two persons aged over 10.

official_measurement_examples.name: Child sleeping room minimum
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2018 regulations set 4.64 square metres as the minimum sleeping room floor area for one child under 10 and prohibit use of rooms below 4.64 square metres as sleeping accommodation.

official_measurement_examples.name: HHSRS follow-up
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK says the council must carry out an HHSRS risk assessment on an HMO within 5 years of receiving a licence application.

official_measurement_examples.name: Licensing and planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Government HMO reform guidance encourages coordination between planning and licensing teams, while the two regulatory regimes remain legally distinct.
